news.headline: RTW Investments and Susquehanna disclose new stakes in uniQure in 13G filings
news.summary: RTW Investments reported a beneficial stake of roughly 3.94M shares (about 5.7%) and Susquehanna-affiliated entities disclosed a 3.34M-share (4.8%) position in filings accepted by the SEC on August 14. The disclosures point to continued institutional accumulation ahead of the September AMT-130 four-year data and the Q3 BLA submission.

news.headline: Stifel reiterates Buy on uniQure with $71 price target into the September readout
news.summary: Stifel maintained its Buy rating and $71 target, pointing to the cleared FDA accelerated-approval pathway for AMT-130 and the four-year Phase I/II data as the next major stock catalyst. Sell-side sentiment has stayed broadly constructive since the June FDA reversal, with the consensus target now around $70.

news.headline: uniQure says an FDA advisory committee for AMT-130 is likely and welcomes the scrutiny
news.summary: Chief Medical Officer Walid Abi-Saab said the company considers an advisory committee meeting for its Huntington's gene therapy probable and is preparing for one, even though the FDA has not formally requested it. His comments came as regulatory uncertainty over unpredictable FDA advisory practices spread across biopharma.

news.headline: Wolfe Research upgrades uniQure to Outperform, sees a clear path to approval for AMT-130
news.summary: Wolfe moved to Outperform with a $65 target, arguing the market prices AMT-130 approval odds below 50% while Wolfe models roughly 70%, with peak U.S. sales potential near $2 billion. The upgrade followed the FDA's June agreement to accept three-year data as the primary basis for an accelerated-approval BLA.

news.headline: uniQure reports Q2 2026 results, confirms Q3 BLA timeline and cash runway into 2030
news.summary: Revenue was $5.8M and cash plus investments stood at $810.3M as of June 30 after the $259M June raise, funding operations into 2030, while the net loss widened to $81.1M on commercial-readiness spending. Management said final FDA meeting minutes received in July confirmed the accelerated-approval alignment, kept the AMT-130 BLA and UK MAA on track for Q3 2026, guided to four-year Phase I/II data in September, and detailed the confirmatory study design (randomized standard-of-care control, Total Functional Capacity at 36 months).

news.headline: Roche ends both of its Huntington's disease programs, clearing the field for uniQure
news.summary: Roche discontinued its two remaining Huntington's programs, the Ionis-partnered tominersen and RG6496, after tominersen lowered mutant huntingtin and NfL but failed to slow clinical progression. The exit removes uniQure's most advanced competitor just as AMT-130 heads into its BLA submission.

catalysts.label: Four-year AMT-130 data readout
catalysts.detail: uniQure plans to present four-year follow-up data on all 24 patients from the first two Phase I/II cohorts (12 high-dose, 12 low-dose), plus additional three-year follow-up on three more high-dose patients, from a June 30, 2026 data cut. Stifel and Wolfe both flag this as the key near-term catalyst ahead of the BLA and any advisory committee.

catalysts.label: AMT-130 US BLA submission
catalysts.detail: uniQure remains on track to submit the BLA for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease under the FDA accelerated-approval pathway in Q3 2026, based on final June/July meeting minutes confirming that the three-year analysis can serve as the primary clinical basis.

catalysts.label: UK MHRA marketing authorization application
catalysts.detail: Following a successful MHRA pre-submission meeting, uniQure plans a parallel UK MAA for AMT-130 in Q3 2026 on the same three-year data package, giving a second potential approval route independent of the FDA.

catalysts.label: FDA advisory committee (AdCom) meeting
catalysts.detail: Management believes an advisory committee review is likely for what would be the first gene therapy for Huntington's disease and says it is preparing for one, but the FDA has not confirmed a meeting or a date.

catalysts.label: Confirmatory trial design finalized and initiated
catalysts.detail: The FDA requires a randomized, concurrent standard-of-care-controlled confirmatory study with Total Functional Capacity at 36 months as the primary endpoint; uniQure says it intends to start this global trial as soon as possible after the BLA submission.

catalysts.label: Additional international regulatory pathways
catalysts.detail: uniQure said it is actively pursuing further registration routes for AMT-130 beyond the US and UK and expects to give an update in the second half of 2026.

catalysts.label: Potential accelerated approval decision; AMT-260 and Fabry updates
catalysts.detail: If the BLA is accepted with priority review, an FDA decision on the first potential Huntington's gene therapy could land around mid-2027; uniQure also plans further clinical updates for its AMT-260 refractory temporal lobe epilepsy and Fabry disease programs in H1 2027.

pulse: QURE is still a catalyst-driven, binary story, but the setup has kept improving: the June FDA reversal accepting three-year AMT-130 data for an accelerated-approval BLA was confirmed by final meeting minutes in July, Roche's July 9 exit from Huntington's removed the last late-stage competitor, and the July 29 Q2 print locked in an $810M cash position and runway into 2030. Sell-side sentiment has followed, with Wolfe upgrading to Outperform ($65, ~70% approval odds) and Stifel reiterating Buy at $71, while RTW and Susquehanna disclosed sizeable stakes in mid-August 13G filings. The stock now trades on execution rather than newsflow: the September four-year data readout is the next real test, followed by the Q3 US BLA and UK MAA filings and a likely-but-unconfirmed FDA advisory committee, and after the summer run-up any data softness or contentious AdCom is the main downside risk.
